title: GlossoGen: Emergent Language in Complex Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
one_sentence: In a complex AI–AI task, character pressure plus explicitly prompted postmortem coordination produces efficient dyad-specific shorthand, partial productivity, newcomer uptake, and metalinguistic repair.
problem: Under what task, model, and interaction conditions do pretrained LLM agents develop, use, and transmit communication protocols beyond ordinary English?
method: GlossoGen's two-agent SaveVeyru task combines asymmetric information and action spaces with 15-round interactions, character budgets, optional unmetered postmortems, multiple proprietary/open models, productive-form probes, and one-agent swap experiments with 0/1/5/10 rounds of history.
findings: Under tight character budgets, proprietary-model teams with postmortems produced less English-like shorthand and outperformed comparable no-postmortem teams; open-weight teams did not reliably develop such protocols.
Newcomer success increased with the amount of prior message-and-action history, and newcomers asked fewer clarification questions about compositional terms as history increased.
The paper reports partial productive structure and transmission, but only one replacement generation was tested.
real_contribution: Provides a richer protocol-development testbed than fixed-role reference games by combining asymmetric roles, explicit meta-coordination, action consequences, partner replacement, history dosage, and repair-like queries.
biggest_weakness: The system prompt explicitly tells agents to develop shorthand, postmortems permit free code definition, several linguistic measures depend on LLM judges, and one swap cannot establish cumulative cultural evolution.
claim_boundary: Supports prompted AI–AI protocol negotiation and partial newcomer uptake, not spontaneous convention, human-like common ground, human–AI interaction, physical embodiment, or cumulative cultural evolution.
why_researcher_should_care: It supplies concrete lifecycle components—explicit negotiation, history dosage, partner swap, active clarification, and transfer—that can be adapted into stricter human–embodied-AI experiments with counterfactual history controls.

amsc.master_list_decision: Candidate — Important / AI–AI protocol lifecycle and diagnostic precedent

evidence_notes: Open arXiv HTML/full text inspected; v1 submitted 2026-09-01.
The paper's cumulative-cultural-evolution claim is treated as overreach because the experiment includes only one newcomer swap rather than multiple successive generations.
